questions.explanation: The relationship is: object → the place where it is kept/displayed. Books are stored and accessed in a Library; Paintings are displayed and preserved in a Museum. B (Canvas) is the surface a painting is made on. C (Frame) is a border, not a location. D (Artist) is the creator. Pattern: artefact → its dedicated institution.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: Rule: n → n². Verify: 8² = 64 ✓. Applying to 5: 5² = 25. **Short Trick:** Square the second number: 8²=64, so 5²=25. Watch out for D (=5×4) and C (=5×6) which are wrong operations.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: The relationship is: tool → the activity it performs. A Pen is used for Writing; a Brush is used for Painting. A (Color) is what paint is, not the activity. B (Artist) is the person, not the activity. D (Canvas) is the surface, not the activity. The analogy maps tool → activity.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: Rule: (a, b) → a² + b². Verify: 2² + 3² = 4 + 9 = 13 ✓. Apply to (4, 5): 4² + 5² = 16 + 25 = 41. **Short Trick:** Sum of squares. A (35=4²+3²+3... no, 35≠41). D=41 is the only option matching 16+25. Distractors: 35=(4+5)×... doesn't fit; 37 is a prime near 41 but incorrect.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: Rule: Reverse the letter sequence. ABCD reversed = DCBA ✓. MNOP reversed: M-N-O-P → P-O-N-M = PONM. B (OPNM) reverses only the first and last letters incorrectly. C (NOPQ) shifts forward by one. D (PMON) scrambles without a clear rule. Reversal is a common exam pattern — write the word backwards.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: The relationship is antonyms/opposites in physical geography. A Mountain's opposite (lowest point between mountains) is a Valley; a Peak's opposite (lowest point of a wave or landform) is a Trough. A (Hill) is a smaller Mountain, not its opposite. C (Rock) and D (Cliff) are unrelated opposites. Peak : Trough is a standard physics/geography pair.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: Rule: n² → n (square root). Verify: √144 = 12 ✓ (12² = 144). Apply: √256 = 16 (16² = 256). **Short Trick:** Recognise perfect squares. 12²=144, 13²=169, 14²=196, 15²=225, 16²=256. A (14) gives 196, B (18) gives 324 — both wrong. Answer is 16.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: Rule: Each letter in the second group is exactly 1 step ahead of the corresponding letter in the first group. B+1=C, D+1=E, F+1=G ✓. Apply to MOQ: M(13)+1=N(14), O(15)+1=P(16), Q(17)+1=R(18) → NPR. A (NQS) shifts Q and S by +2. B (NPQ) incorrect last letter. C (NOR) incorrect middle letter. NPR=D is correct.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: The relationship is: container → what it primarily holds/contains. A Cup is associated with Coffee; a Bowl is associated with Soup (soup is the most typical content of a bowl). B (Glass) is another container, not a content. C (Plate) and D (Utensil) are not contents. The pattern is vessel → typical content.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: Rule: n → n². Verify: 7² = 49 ✓. Apply: 9² = 81. **Short Trick:** Square the number: 9×9=81. A (63=7×9 or 9×7) and C (72=8×9) represent wrong operations. D (90=9×10) is also wrong. Memorise: 7²=49, 8²=64, 9²=81, 10²=100.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: The relationship is: collective noun → what it is a collection of. An Archipelago is a group of Islands; an Anthology is a collection of Literary works (poems, short stories, essays, or other writings). A (Poets) and B (Authors) are the creators, not the works themselves. D (Songs) is a subset but 'literary works' is the more precise and general answer.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: Rule: Each pair of corresponding letters sums to 27 (A=1+Z=26=27; C=3+X=24=27; E=5+V=22=27). This is the 'complementary pair' pattern. Apply to GIK: G=7 → 27−7=20=T; I=9 → 27−9=18=R; K=11 → 27−11=16=P → TRP. Order matters: T,R,P = TRP (D). A (TPR) and B (RTP) are scrambled versions. Answer: D=TRP.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: The relationship is: professional → the event/act that defines their public performance. A Surgeon performs an Operation; a Musician performs at a Concert. B (Stage) is the venue, not the event. C (Instrument) is the tool, not the act. D (Orchestra) is the group, not the event. The pattern is professional → their characteristic professional event.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: Rule: n → n × (n+1). Verify: 7 × 8 = 56 ✓. Apply to 9: 9 × 10 = 90. **Short Trick:** Multiply n by (n+1) — the next consecutive number. A (72=8×9, wrongly uses 8 as base). C (81=9²—squares n instead). D (99=9×11—skips n+1). Only B=90 gives 9×10 correctly.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: The relationship is: physical phenomenon → the instrument that measures it. Light intensity is measured by a Photometer; Sound intensity (hearing threshold) is measured by an Audiometer. A (Thermometer) measures temperature. B (Barometer) measures atmospheric pressure. D (Galvanometer) measures small electric currents. Audiometers are used by ENT specialists to assess hearing.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: Rule: n → n² + 1. Verify: 3²+1=9+1=10 ✓; 7²+1=49+1=50 ✓. Apply to 5: 5²+1=25+1=26. **Short Trick:** Square n then add 1. A (30=5²+5), B (24=5²−1), C (28=5²+3) are all wrong offsets. Only D=26 fits n²+1. The pattern tests whether students add 1 or some other constant.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: Rule: The first letter stays in place; positions 2, 3, 4 undergo a cyclic shift where the last letter moves to position 2. DEAR(D,E,A,R): D stays; E,A,R → R,E,A → DREA ✓. Apply to NEAT(N,E,A,T): N stays; E,A,T → T,E,A → NTEA. B (ANTE) is a rearrangement of NEAT's letters but wrong pattern. C (NATE) keeps N and shifts only one letter. D (ATEN) is a different scrambling. Answer: A=NTEA.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: The relationship is: specialist → the organ they treat. A Dentist treats the Teeth; a Cardiologist treats the Heart (cardio = relating to the heart). A (Lungs) → Pulmonologist; C (Kidneys) → Nephrologist; D (Brain) → Neurologist. The analogy is medical specialist → area of specialisation.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: Rule: n → √n. Verify: √16 = 4 ✓. Apply: √64 = 8 (since 8² = 64). **Short Trick:** Take the square root. 4²=16, 8²=64. A (4) is wrong because √64=8≠4. B (6): 6²=36≠64. D (10): 10²=100≠64. Answer: C=8.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.stem: In a certain code, TREE is written as QOBB. Using the same code, FOREST is written as:
questions.explanation: Rule: Each letter is shifted −3 (three positions back). T(20)−3=Q(17), R(18)−3=O(15), E(5)−3=B(2), E(5)−3=B(2) → QOBB ✓. Apply to FOREST: F(6)−3=C(3), O(15)−3=L(12), R(18)−3=O(15), E(5)−3=B(2), S(19)−3=P(16), T(20)−3=Q(17) → CLOBPQ. Answer: D=CLOBPQ. Distractors differ in specific letter positions — verify each letter individually.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: Rule: n → n³ + n. Verify: 6³ + 6 = 216 + 6 = 222 ✓. Apply to 5: 5³ + 5 = 125 + 5 = 130. **Short Trick:** Cube n then add n itself. B (125=5³ only, forgot to add 5). C (135=5³+10, added 2n). D (120=5³−5, subtracted instead). Only A=130 fits n³+n exactly.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: The relationship is: medical specialist → the organ they treat. An Ophthalmologist specialises in the Eyes; a Nephrologist specialises in the Kidneys (nephros = kidney in Greek). A (Nerves) → Neurologist; C (Liver) → Hepatologist; D (Lungs) → Pulmonologist. The key root to remember: nephro- = kidney (as in nephron, the basic kidney unit).
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: Rule: Each pair shifts one letter forward — the second letter of the first pair becomes the first letter of the next pair. AB → BC (A+1=B; B+1=C). BC → CD. CD → DE. So CD:DE follows the same pattern. The sequence is: AB, BC, CD, DE, EF... Answer: C=DE. A (CE) skips a letter. B (CF) skips two. D (EF) skips CD entirely.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: The relationship is: tool → the professional who uses it. A Scalpel is used by a Surgeon; a Gavel (the small wooden mallet used to call order in a court or auction) is used by a Judge. A (Carpenter) uses a hammer, not a gavel. B (Lawyer) argues cases but does not wield the gavel — the judge does. C (Policeman) uses a baton. Answer: D=Judge.
questions.subject: reasoning

questions.explanation: Rule: Each letter in the second group is exactly 1 ahead of the corresponding letter in the first group. E+1=F, G+1=H, I+1=J, K+1=L → FHJL ✓. Apply to BDFH: B(2)+1=C(3), D(4)+1=E(5), F(6)+1=G(7), H(8)+1=I(9) → CEGI. A (CEIG) has I and G swapped. B (DFGI) shifts by 2. D (CEGJ) has wrong last letter (J=10≠I=9). Answer: C=CEGI.
questions.subject: reasoning
